links.note: Two of the three sub-questions are modes of occurrence - a mineral formed by decomposition of rocks leaving a residual mass, and minerals deposited in the strata of sedimentary rocks. Both are 23979's description. The bauxite answer touches 23984 but the question asked is about how it forms, not what it yields.
Nagercoil and Jaisalmer for wind energy is 23992's content; the distractors solar, atomic and tidal separate it from 23993 and from the atomic material this frame has no concept for.
Assam and Gujarat holding most of India's petroleum deposits - 23991. 23990 Coal is the neighbouring fossil-fuel concept but no coalfield is in the options.
Assam as the oldest oil-producing state (Digboi, Naharkatiya, Moran-Hugrijan) sits in the petroleum passage, 23991.

Magnesium being largely derived from ocean water is the ocean-water clause of the modes-of-occurrence passage (common salt, magnesium and bromine from sea water), so 23979. The distractors bauxite, gold and mica are land minerals, which is the discrimination.
Peat as the coal form with low carbon, high moisture and low heating capacity is the grades-of-coal passage in 23990, against lignite, bituminous and anthracite from the same ladder.
